October 2025 NEWS FROM THE BOARDNEWS FROM THE BOARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners November 2025 Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. Ryan Davidson - Commissioner Rod Beck - Chairman Tom Dayley - Commissioner SAYING GOODBYE TO 2025 THE ONLY CONSTANT IS CHANGE This time of year, makes a lot of us nostalgic for days gone by. These photos taken in November of the Ada County Courthouse on Front Street in downtown Boise remind us of how quickly time flies. January 20, 2026 is the 26-year anniversary of the groundbreaking for this impressive facility. The building was completed in 2002. If you’ve lived in this area for more than twenty years you can see the dramatic change to our skyline. It’s nice that you can still see the Idaho Statehouse from this vantage point. If you want to see the previous Ada County Courthouse, which was built in 1939, you can check out the Art Deco style building that still stands at the 514 West Jefferson Street. The Ada County Commissioners wish you, your friends and loved ones a very Merry Christmas and a happy, safe and prosperous New Year. The Ada County Courthouse is a LEED-certified building, having achieved Silver certification in May 2005 for its existing building operations and maintenance. It was the first building in Idaho to register and receive *LEED certification. *Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design is a globally recognized green building certification program. The system evaluates buildings on things like energy efficiency, water conservation, waste reduction and indoor environmental quality. 1

ADA COUNTY RECOGNIZES NEW FAMILIES WITH ADOPTION MONTH Every year the Ada County Commissioners sign a proclamation recognizing November as Adoption Month. It’s a month to honor and recognize the new families that are created through adoption. To mark the occasion, every year the Trial Court Administrator’s Office (TCA) organizes a wonderful celebration here at the courthouse. The annual event is spearheaded by Office Manager Tia Andrews. Ada County employees donate gift baskets for the children being adopted. We are also fortunate to have the non-profit organization Community Cakes, donate the cakes that look like delicious works of art. Thank you to all the Ada County employees who generously pitched in to create some amazing gift baskets. Congratulations to the families that are now a little bigger and filled with even more love. HIGH HONORS FOR THE ADA COUNTY CLERK’S OFFICE The Ada County Auditor’s Office was recently awarded the Certificate of Achievement for Excellence in Financial Reporting for its annual comprehensive financial report for the fiscal year that ended September 30, 2024. The Certificate of Achievement is the highest honor in governmental accounting and financial reporting. According to the Government Finance Officers Association (GFOA), the report was judged by an impartial panel to meet the high standards of the program This means demonstrating a constructive spirit of full disclosure—clearly communicating its financial story and encouraging potential users and user groups to engage with the report. Congratulations to everyone who contributed to achieving this accomplishment! Nicole Newby Public Information Officer Ada County Clerk’s Office Pictured L-R: Malinda Kempton - Senior Accountant , Ryan Thurman - Internal Auditor Mandy Guinn - Senior Accountant, Heath Ribordy - Assistant Chief Deputy Clerk, Tom Dayley - Ada County Commissioner, Jena Vaughn - Senior Accountant, Kimberly Edwards - Senior Accountant, Sarah Lund - Accounting Manager, Tim Sturges - Controller, Trent Tripple - Ada County Clerk, Rod Beck - Ada County Commission Chairman, Ryan Davidson - Ada County Commissioner, Dawn Bridge - Grant Administrator, Katie Reed - Chief Deputy Clerk 3

SKATEBOARDERS THROUGHOUT THE NORTHWEST HAVE A TREAT IN STORE New world-class all wheel facility being built in Ada County will be a game changer Skateboarding is gaining in popularity every year and was one of the competitive sports at last year’s Summer Olympics in Paris. Wheel-sports of all kinds, including skateboarding, rollerblading, and roller derby, have die-hard fan bases. These folks are athletes who take their sport very seriously. We love showing you the progress on The Park at Expo Idaho. This month we have significant progress to show you one of the park’s most interesting features - the all-wheel area. The company that designed the Skateboarding venue for the Olympics, California Skateparks, designed this new area. If you know any avid skateboarders or roller bladers, and they don’t already know what’s going in at The Park at Expo Idaho – let them know! Have them follow us on Facebook for frequent updates. The skatepark going in right alongside 4 the Boise River will be one of the largest skateparks in the Northwest. The entire Park at Expo Idaho is scheduled to open in late summer of next year. Thank you to the Ada County Commissioners - Chairman Rod Beck, Commissioner Ryan Davidson, and Commissioner Tom Dayley for making this park a reality. Photos: Michael McCullough

OPERATION GREEN LIGHT FOR VETERANS On Tuesday, November 11, 2025 Ada County participated in a nationwide effort to recognize one of our country’s most celebrated holidays. Across the country, counties and parishes lit up their courthouse exteriors in green. It’s part of an initiative called “Operation Green Light for Veterans”. By shining a green light, county governments let veterans in our communities know that they are seen, appreciated, and supported. Veterans Day is a federal holiday dedicated to honoring all who have served in the U.S. Armed Forces, recognizing their service and sacrifice. 5

# Page 6^page=6
ADA COUNTY COMMISSIONERS TAKE PART IN THE ANNUAL VETERANS DAY PARADE A bright and sunny day greeted enthusiastic attendees at the annual Idaho Veterans Parade in Downtown Boise. The Ada County Commissioners—Ryan Davidson, Chairman Rod Beck, and Commissioner Tom Dayley — were honored to take part in the parade, as they do each year. The mission of the Idaho Veterans Parade is to recognize the sacrifices and honor the service of all veterans of the United States Armed Forces and to heighten community awareness, appreciation, and value of military service to our nation. This year’s parade commemorated the 50th anniversary of the end of the Vietnam War. More than 58,000 United States service members died in that nineteen-year war that ended officially in 1975. Special thanks to photographer and Veteran, Dan Murphy, for the photos 6

# Page 7^page=7
ADA COUNTY EMPLOYEES VOLUNTEER THEIR TIME TO RAKE UP NEIGHBORHOODS Enthusiastic Ada County employees turned out again this year, volunteering a Saturday to Rake up Boise. The event is organized each year by NeighborWorks Boise. The organization tells us total of 557 yards were raked using multiple volunteer teams. So, how do homes qualify for this altruistic service? To qualify, homes must be in Boise, Eagle, Garden City, Kuna or Meridian, the resident must be 65 or older, or disabled, and must be unable to maintain their yard due to physical or financial constraints. This event has been going for over 40 years! Thank you to everyone who volunteered to be part of Ada County’s Team! 7

Thank you to Leadership Meridian for inviting Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson to speak to this year’s class about county government. These presentations are a good opportunity to help future leaders understand the role of county government in their lives. Commissioner Davidson’s presentation included information on what services the State of Idaho mandates that counties provide to residents, as well as where your property tax dollars go. When you pay your property taxes the lion’s share goes to cities, and schools. Approximately 50% of Ada County property taxes go toward public safety. See the pie chart below. 8

MAKING THINGS EASIER FOR YOU HOWEVER WE CAN You’re busy. We’re making things easier. The Ada County Assessor’s Office is now offering you the option to renew your vehicle registration virtually. This service provides all the benefits of renewing in-office, but with the added convenience of using your phone or computer from anywhere. Learn how easy it is: NEW IDAHO VIRTUAL DMV - HERE’S HOW IT WORKS You’ve been following along as we show you progress videos for The Park at Expo Idaho, scheduled to open late summer of next year. So, what’s this structure, you ask? That is the playground pavilion. It includes a large men’s restroom, a large women’s restroom, and two family restrooms. The pavilion will also feature three large picnic tables, comfortable benches just outside the perimeter, and a misting garden. The main park wayfinding signage will be mounted beneath the oculus. 9

LOOKING AHEAD TO OUR DECEMBER 2025 NEWSLETTER Our last newsletter of 2025 comes out in late December. What a year 2025 has been and do we have great things in store for 2026! Coming up next month, we’ll be looking ahead to some of the exciting projects happening in Ada County in the coming year. One of the biggest initiatives is America250 – a nationwide celebration of the 250 anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. We’ll tell you how Ada County plans to celebrate. Our Christmas wish this year is that you share this newsletter with your friends and neighbors so they can keep track of what’s happening in our communities. It’s easy to sign up using the QR code. ADA COUNTY GOVERNMENT In addition to elected offices, Ada County government includes twelve individual departments. Each department provides important services to our residents in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Boise, Garden City, Kuna, and Unincorporated Ada County. These services include law enforcement protection, emergency preparedness, election services, parks & waterways, indigent services, juvenile services, solid waste management, the Western Idaho Fair, Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement and more. Learn more about the services provided to you by Ada County - www.adacounty.id.gov/ 10
